experiment.name: DTMF Signal Simulation and Analysis
experiment.description: Simulation of DTMF tone generation, spectral analysis, noise effects, spectral resolution, automatic decoding, and line attenuation.

noise_analysis.description: White Gaussian noise is added to the target DTMF tone to evaluate spectral robustness.

duration_analysis.description: Shorter signals provide poorer frequency resolution, while longer observation times improve separation of the DTMF frequency components.

attenuation.description: Amplitude attenuation is applied to the target DTMF signal to simulate transmission losses.

expected_observations: The DTMF digit "5" should contain two dominant frequency components at 770 Hz and 1336 Hz.
The time-domain signal is the sum of two sinusoidal signals.
The FFT should show two dominant spectral peaks corresponding to the low and high DTMF groups.
Increasing SNR should make the two DTMF spectral peaks easier to distinguish.
Decreasing tone duration reduces FFT frequency resolution.
Line attenuation reduces signal amplitude but should not change the theoretical DTMF frequencies.
The decoder should identify the sequence "582A*" from the generated signal.

images.expected_features: Noise floor increases as SNR decreases.

images.description: FFT spectrum for different DTMF tone durations.
images.expected_features: Longer signals produce narrower spectral peaks.
